name: Ueno
tagline: Tokyo in 5 minutes and Otemachi in 11 minutes. Served by 8 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Taito City, where JR East and Tokyo Metro run 8 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 11 minutes to Otemachi, 23 minutes to Shinjuku, 30 minutes to Shibuya and 20 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 4.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 15.4 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 4.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2 m to 17.4 m, a difference of 15.4 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 5 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 4 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 51 clinics and 45 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is アイシークリニック上野院, about 5 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 全仁会上野病院, about 5 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 8 lines serve the station. JR Yamanote Line and JR Utsunomiya Line run through it. JR Joban Line and JR Takasaki Line also call here. JR Keihin-Tohoku Line are available too. JR Ueno-Tokyo Line stop here as well. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line stop here as well. Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line stop here as well. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 6 lines and Tokyo Metro runs 2 lines), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line runs at 163% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 三ノ輪→入谷, which this station is not on. JR Keihin-Tohoku Line runs at 159%. Its busiest stretch is 大井町→品川, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line runs at 153%. Its busiest stretch is 赤坂見附→溜池山王, which this station is likewise not on. JR Ueno-Tokyo Line is not covered by the ministry's congestion survey. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000 and 2LDK ¥260,000 to ¥270,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the lowest in the 23 wards. In plain yen, though, it is on the high side for the 23 wards. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Keisei-Ueno is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Ueno is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ueno. It takes 17 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Ueno.

neighbours.lead: Inaricho is ahead on quiet, but Ueno is ahead on the number of lines and how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ueno. It takes 5 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Ueno. One-room rents run about ¥7,000 higher.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: The data does not show a drawback particular to this station
noiseSources: The 首都高速1号上野線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
昭和通り (2 lanes each way) runs just outside the station. In a flat facing it, the cars are audible morning and evening

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 22 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: 8 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the lowest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are some of the most heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
